A trigger button starts a rapidly counting counter that slows down to simulate a dice roll-off. Two LEDs indicate the pulse count during counting and signal when the result is ready. The design is implemented in Verilog and uses a 7-segment display plus two LEDs as external hardware.

results.summary_before: This project implements Conway's Game of Life as a cellular automaton. It outputs a VGA video signal and renders graphics on a display. The design is notable for its real-time simulation and visual output. It is intended for educational or recreational purposes.
results.summary: This project is a fully self-contained MNIST handwritten-digit classifier implemented as a ternary-weight MLP with all weights baked into the netlist as Verilog constants. It accepts 64 binarized 8x8 pixel bits serially and computes a digit prediction in about 172 clock cycles at 10 MHz. The predicted digit is output on uio[3:0] and shown on the on-board 7-segment display, with DONE and BUSY status pins. The design is written in Verilog and was verified with a cocotb testbench against 200 MNIST images.

results.summary_before: This project is a 2-bit flash analog-to-digital converter that converts an analog input voltage between 0 and 1.8 V into a 2-bit encoded digital output. The design uses comparators to compare the input against reference voltages and encodes the results. It is implemented in analog and is a simple example of a flash ADC. The output is provided on two dedicated digital pins.
results.summary: This project is a 4x4 structural array multiplier implemented in Verilog. It takes two 4-bit binary inputs and produces an 8-bit product by combining partial products with full adders. The design is purely digital and requires no external hardware. Testing involves applying two 4-bit values and reading the resulting product on the eight output pins.

results.summary: This project implements a digital leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron in Verilog. It takes four weight inputs and a spike input, and produces a spike output. The neuron uses reset-by-subtraction and has configurable leakage and threshold settings. No external hardware is required, and testing consists of applying weights and a spike input and observing whether the neuron spikes.

results.summary_before: KianV RISC-V RV32E Baremetal SoC is a bare-metal RV32E RISC-V system-on-chip with a UART, a QSPI memory controller for PSRAM and flash, a generic SPI interface, a sigma-delta audio emulator and PWM output. It is designed for embedded applications and can be programmed via the UART or SPI. The SoC includes a memory controller for external PSRAM and flash. It is notable for its small footprint and bare-metal operation.
results.summary: This project is a software-defined radio pipeline for AM radio reception written in Verilog. It uses an external comparator as a 1-bit ADC frontend that is oversampled and decimated 4096 times to gain about 6 bits of precision. A SPI interface with a single 32-bit shift register sets the NCO phase increment for tuning and the gain, and the demodulated signal is output as PWM audio. External hardware includes a comparator, resistor bias network, RC network, RF amplifier and an SPI microcontroller.
